common_conditions: XCAP referenced by TS24.481 V19.3.0; RFC4825 rules
condition_rule: Inherit common_conditions and add claim conditions.

claims.conclusion: Document PUT uses application-usage MIME and whole-document replacement; element body contains the complete element and its content, not a partial merge, and uses application/xcap-el+xml, attribute body uses application/xcap-att+xml and XML AttValue without URI percent encoding.

Creation selector is currently no-match but must select inserted object afterwards; replacement must select both old and new object. Changing an identifying attribute selected by its old value can fail with 409.
After deletion the selector must not select a different remaining element; server rejects such deletion with 409 and must not delete.
Schema, uniqueness and other application-usage constraints can independently cause 409 rejection. 409 alone does not identify a group-ID collision.

limitations: Referenced RFC is not itself a Release19 standard.
MCX application schema, complete request headers and authorization are not established by these generic rules.
